claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor inherent oxygen resistance and undergoes accelerated oxidation during high-temperature exposure.
A uniform ultra-thin alumina coating can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by atomic layer deposition or another surface-engineering process.
The deposited alumina coating will form a continuous and adherent surface layer.
A continuous alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier at the alloy surface.
The alumina coating will inhibit rapid oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will provide a stable, slow-growing protective oxide scale.
Limiting oxygen ingress will reduce internal oxidation and preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air for approximately 100 hours, coated HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit markedly reduced oxygen uptake relative to untreated material.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air for approximately 100 hours, coated HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit reduced oxidation corrosion relative to untreated material.
The coated and exposed alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within 8–16%.
The coated alloy will retain a yield strength within 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The coating is expected to remain effective near 1000 °C for exposure times up to approximately 100 hours.
Temperatures significantly above 1000 °C may degrade the coating's performance.
Prolonged thermal cycling may degrade the coating's performance.
Severe mechanical deformation may cause the protective alumina layer to spall.
